status_summary: SBA announced on 2025-07-14 (news release 25-62) that it eliminated a regulation that made entities principally engaged in teaching, counseling or indoctrinating religion ineligible for Economic Injury Disaster Loans, effective immediately, and launched a Center for Faith. This matches part of the Mandate's recommendation for disaster loans. The release does not name a CFR section and does not mention Form 1971, business loan programs or a 28 U.S.C. 530D notice, and no Federal Register rule or notice for the change was found; a Center for Public Justice analysis (2025-08-17) describes the repeal as made without a comment period and asks whether that fits administrative procedure rules. Federal Register searches still show the 2021-01-19 proposed rule and the 2022 business-loan rule as the only rulemaking documents on the subject, the eCFR shows no amendments to 13 CFR part 123 from July to December 2025, and part 120 changed only for penalty and enforcement provisions on 2025-06-03. SBA's final rule of 2026-09-29 (91 FR 61295) removes affirmative-action and disparate-impact provisions from 13 CFR part 112 and does not address religious eligibility. Whether Form 1971 was withdrawn or is still used was not verified.

title: Remove religious-entity exclusions from SBA loan programs and retire Form 1971
uncertainties: The only primary evidence of the 2025 change is SBA's own news release, which does not say what legal vehicle was used. The Center for Public Justice analysis names the repealed provision as a section in 13 CFR part 120, but the eCFR amendment history for parts 120 and 123 shows no matching change, so the CFR citation and mechanism are unresolved (it may have been a non-enforcement or policy decision rather than a codified repeal). The July 2025 change is reported for disaster loans; the analysis says religious businesses can also now receive SBA loans, which the release does not state. SBA's forms page for Form 1971 returned an access error, so whether the form was withdrawn is unknown; a Federal Register listing of SBA documents from 2025-06-16 to 2025-07-29 contained no rule or notice on religious eligibility. An OMB-led proposed rule on federal financial assistance (2026-05-29), which lists SBA among about 40 issuing agencies, concerns grants and cooperative agreements (2 CFR) and was not found to address SBA loan eligibility. A 530D letter would not appear in the Federal Register. Searches run: SBA Form 1971 and religious eligibility 2025 to 2026; SBA July 2025 repeal of religious ineligibility rule; plus Federal Register API queries and eCFR amendment histories.
